sources.sourceTitle: What to Bring — National Park Service
sources.text: Plan for a tent, sleeping pad, and sleeping bag suited to the location and season. A tent’s stated capacity describes sleeping space; account separately for gear or pets. Choose bedding for the conditions and your own needs, and keep dry clothes for bedtime. Check local rules before relying on a hammock or shelter tied to trees.

sources.text: Use a packing checklist that covers navigation, sun protection, extra clothing, lighting, first-aid supplies, fire-starting supplies where permitted, repair tools, extra food, water and treatment supplies, and emergency shelter. Adapt it to your activity and conditions; it is a starting point, not a complete equipment list. Pack a headlamp and spare batteries, plus layers for changing weather.

sources.sourceTitle: Before the Trip — National Park Service
sources.text: Choose a campsite and activities that fit everyone’s experience and ability. Consider the season, access on foot or by car, and trip length when packing. Leave your route, departure details, expected return, and park emergency contact with someone staying home. Prepare an alternative plan if conditions make your original trip unsuitable. Practice with unfamiliar equipment before leaving.
sources.title: Plan a manageable first trip
